candidates.title: Preserve the control codebook's pairwise geometry
candidates.falsifier: Measure codebook pairwise-distance distortion, transition endpoint codeword separation, level-wise occupancy, hard-SID churn, and the single frozen Stage-3 evaluation against control. The mechanism is falsified as a useful candidate if it fails to reduce geometry distortion or pair convergence, or if it changes SIDs without improving downstream recall@10 or NDCG@10.
candidates.risk: The regularizer may preserve a codebook geometry that is suboptimal for the treatment's learned representations, or its weight may be too weak to prevent codebook drift. Conversely, even modest movement in codeword positions can change nearest-code assignments discontinuously, so preserved pairwise geometry does not ensure preserved useful item assignments or improved Stage-3 retrieval.
candidates.codebook_interaction: Each codeword receives gradients from its distances to all other codewords, pulling the trainable pairwise distance matrix toward the frozen control distance matrix. A transition's two codewords are not treated as a pair in the loss: there is no endpoint-pair attraction, and the reference distances penalize their converging below their control separation. The term can still move codes and alter hard assignments; it does not guarantee that assignments stay fixed.

candidates.title: Discourage behaviour-near transitions from sharing level-zero codes
candidates.falsifier: At the probe, check that the term produces a nonzero codebook gradient and reduces behaviour-weighted soft assignment overlap without reducing transition endpoint codeword separation or collapsing occupancy. The candidate is falsified if it fails to change hard SIDs, collapses or sharply concentrates level-zero usage, or the frozen Stage-3 recall@10/NDCG@10 do not improve over control.
candidates.risk: Assignment exclusion may force behaviour-similar transitions into arbitrary different codes, damaging item neighbourhoods and recommendation ranking, or may spread probability across codes without changing hard assignments. If the temperature or weight makes gradients concentrate on a few codes, it could also destabilize occupancy or indirectly reduce endpoint codeword separation despite having no explicit attraction term.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The loss penalizes overlap between the endpoints' soft assignment distributions, not their codeword distance. Its codebook gradients arise through both endpoint assignment probabilities and push their probability mass toward different codes. It contains no term that attracts the two selected codewords; it can nevertheless indirectly move codewords in ways that reduce separation, so probe measurements must check endpoint codeword distances and occupancy.

candidates.title: Align residual codebook displacement with behaviour-conditioned item displacement
candidates.falsifier: Measure the behaviour-weighted residual-displacement error, level-wise codebook movement, transition endpoint codeword separations, occupancy, hard-SID churn, and the one frozen Stage-3 evaluation. The candidate is falsified if its codebook gradient does not reduce the specified residual error, if endpoint separation or occupancy collapses, or if Stage-3 recall@10 and NDCG@10 fail to improve over control.
candidates.risk: The behaviour-weighted residual differences may be noisy or poorly represented by level-one codewords, and fitting them may distort residual code geometry or create unstable assignments at later levels. Since the loss has no direct encoder gradient and relies on fixed assignments for each evaluation, it may move codewords without making the resulting hard SID structure more useful for Stage-3 ranking.
candidates.codebook_interaction: With assignments fixed and the residual target stop-gradient detached, only the assigned level-one codewords receive this loss's gradient. The term matches a directed difference between two level-one codewords to an observed residual difference; it does not minimize the distance between the endpoint codewords. The resulting gradients can still reduce their separation for some residual targets, so endpoint separation must be checked in the probe.
